required_edits: Amend the closure-authentication design so every fs-verity-measured closure member and verdict-affecting runtime input is bound by inode—not subsequently resolved through a mutable staging pathname. For example, retain an fd for the measured inode and individually attach that exact inode into the private mount namespace using a file bind mount or open_tree/move_mount equivalent, then freeze the root’s complete directory membership. Add rename/unlink-and-replace-after-verification regressions for ld.so, a DT_NEEDED library, git/credential helpers, and CA inputs; the replacement inode must never be executed or read. Clarify the distinct ordinary-content and fs-verity digest pins, then re-freeze and re-authorize the resulting plan hash.
hard_stops: The asserted mutation-point binding for the authenticated dynamic/exec closure is incomplete: fs-verity protects an inode’s contents but explicitly still permits rename, deletion, and linking. A concurrent same-user writer can rename or unlink a verified verity file in the plain staging directory and replace its pathname with an unauthenticated inode before ld.so, a helper, or the trust-store consumer opens it. The existing overwrite regressions do not exercise this pathname-rebinding attack, so the plan does not presently prove that the bytes read or executed are the bytes authenticated.
rationale: I recomputed the candidate identity as sha256:6ffb206daf0599e7daad05647e8b45b44166fefa5aab43bfb7238d07ad297283 and confirmed the plan bytes are unchanged from reviewed head 3b5b437f265f85ef26b0bd0d2e9c39d3a9b19160. The prior x32 defect is correctly repaired by rejecting __X32_SYSCALL_BIT before native syscall-number matching. I explicitly ratify SPIKE-E6-EVALUATOR-FORM and product-1-oq-e6-determinism-deferral: enrollment remains blocked until the constrained declarative grammar and trusted evaluator pass their hard merge gate. I also ratify SPIKE-PD001-NOLISTENER-COMPLETENESS and product-1-oq-pd001-nolistener-completeness as scoped after the x32 correction; exhaustive residual syscall auditing may remain an implementation spike with fail-closed detection. Neither deferral covers this separate tool-closure authentication flaw. The Linux kernel documentation states that verity files remain renameable, deletable, and linkable, confirming that fs-verity alone does not bind a verified inode to the pathname later consumed by the loader: [Linux fs-verity documentation](https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/filesystems/fsverity.html). Because authoritative git, Node, and gh verdicts depend on that closure, pathname substitution can fabricate a trusted verdict despite matching pre-execution measurements. Authorization must therefore remain blocked until the exact measured inodes—not mutable names—are mounted into the execution root.
